docs.title: mcp-searchable
docs.text:
mcp-searchable is a local-first Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that helps AI agents perform practical web research:

  • Search with multiple providers (duckduckgo, google, bing, brave)
  • Fetch pages and convert them into readable Markdown
  • Stash useful content into local SQLite storage
  • Grep stashed content with FTS5
  • Ask questions over local context using Ollama

It is built for reproducible, tool-based research flows where the agent can both gather and reuse context.

docs.title: What does it do?
docs.text:
• Standardizes web search output across providers into { title, url, snippet }
  • Extracts readable content from raw web pages
  • Persists page content locally so agents can reuse it later
  • Enables local semantic workflows without depending on hosted vector services

docs.title: Why mcp-searchable?
docs.text:
Most agent workflows lose context between searches and page reads. mcp-searchable gives agents a persistent local knowledge loop:

  1. discover sources (web_search)
  2. extract content (web_fetch)
  3. store useful material (web_stash)
  4. retrieve relevant context (web_grep)
  5. synthesize answers (web_ask)

docs.title: 1) web_search fails for API-backed providers
docs.text:
• Issue: web_search works with duckduckgo, but fails with google, bing, or brave.
  • Cause: Missing or invalid provider credentials.
  • Fix:
  • google requires GOOGLE_API_KEY and GOOGLE_CSE_ID
  • bing requires BING_API_KEY
  • brave requires BRAVE_API_KEY

After updating .env, restart your MCP client/host process.

docs.title: 2) web_ask fails to answer
docs.text:
• Issue: web_ask returns an error or times out.
  • Cause: Ollama is not running, wrong OLLAMA_URL, or unavailable model.
  • Fix:
  • Ensure Ollama is running and reachable
  • Verify OLLAMA_URL and OLLAMA_MODEL
  • Retry after confirming local Ollama health

docs.title: 3) Low-quality answers from web_ask
docs.text:
• Issue: Answers are vague or miss key details.
  • Cause: Insufficient or noisy stashed context.
  • Fix:
  • Stash higher-quality, relevant sources
  • Use web_grep before web_ask to confirm context quality

docs.title: 4) DuckDuckGo returns fewer results
docs.text:
• Issue: Fewer results than expected with provider=duckduckgo.
  • Cause: HTML endpoint variability and anti-bot response differences.
  • Fix:
  • Retry query with refined terms
  • Use google, bing, or brave for consistent API-backed retrieval

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Node.js 22+
  • npm 10+
  • Python 3.11+
  • uv

Tip

If you use mise, run mise run deps:sync to install toolchain and dependencies.

docs.title: Install from npm (recommended)
docs.text:
npm i -g @dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable

Or use npx from your MCP client configuration:

npx -y @dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable.git mcp-searchable
cd mcp-searchable
npm install
uv sync

docs.title: Configure environment
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env

Fill the provider credentials you plan to use:

  • GOOGLE_API_KEY + GOOGLE_CSE_ID for Google
  • BING_API_KEY (and optional BING_API_ENDPOINT) for Bing
  • BRAVE_API_KEY for Brave

No key is required for duckduckgo.

docs.title: Run the server locally
docs.text:
npm run build
npm start

The server runs over stdio for MCP clients.

docs.title: Verify docs build
docs.text: uv run mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Setup with LLMs
docs.text: Configure your MCP client to launch mcp-searchable over stdio.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text: claude mcp add mcp-searchable -- npx -y @dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable

docs.title: Cursor
docs.text:
Add to ~/.cursor/mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mcp-searchable": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Windsurf
docs.text:
Add to your Windsurf MCP configuration:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mcp-searchable": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: OpenCode
docs.text:
Add to ~/.config/opencode/config.json:

{
  "mcp": {
    "mcp-searchable": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@dragoscirjan/mcp-searchable"]
    }
  }
}

Warning

If you run locally from source instead of npm package, ensure your .env is loaded in the process environment so provider keys are available.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: This is the canonical end-user flow for mcp-searchable.

docs.title: Workflow: Search → Fetch → Stash → Grep → Ask
1) Search
docs.text:
Call web_search to find candidate sources.

{
  "query": "mcp server security best practices",
  "provider": "duckduckgo",
  "limit": 5
}

docs.title: 2) Fetch
docs.text:
Take a result URL and call web_fetch to extract readable Markdown.

{
  "url": "https://example.com/mcp-security"
}

docs.title: 3) Stash
docs.text:
Persist useful content with web_stash.

{
  "url": "https://example.com/mcp-security",
  "title": "MCP Security Guide",
  "content": "# MCP Security Guide\n..."
}

docs.title: 4) Grep local context
docs.text:
Run web_grep to locate relevant stashed snippets.

{
  "query": "token handling",
  "limit": 5
}

docs.title: 5) Ask with local context
docs.text:
Use web_ask for synthesized answers backed by local sources.

{
  "question": "Summarize recommended secret management patterns",
  "limit": 3
}

docs.title: Provider strategy
docs.text:
• Use duckduckgo when you want zero-key quick search.
  • Use google, bing, or brave when you need official API-backed search.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Warning

web_ask requires a running Ollama server reachable at OLLAMA_URL.

Tip

Keep stashed pages focused and high-quality. Better stash quality generally improves web_ask output quality.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: mcp-searchable uses environment variables for search providers and local Q&A.

docs.title: Search providers
docs.text:
Variable Required when Description GOOGLE_API_KEY provider=google API key for Google Custom Search JSON API. GOOGLE_CSE_ID provider=google Custom Search Engine identifier (cx). BING_API_KEY provider=bing API key for Bing Web Search API. BING_API_ENDPOINT optional Override endpoint (default: https://api.bing.microsoft.com/v7.0/search). BRAVE_API_KEY provider=brave API key for Brave Search API.

Tip

duckduckgo works without credentials.

docs.title: Local Q&A (Ollama)
docs.text: Variable Default Description OLLAMA_URL http://localhost:11434 Base URL of Ollama instance. OLLAMA_MODEL llama3 Model used by web_ask.

docs.title: Recommended setup
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env

Then set only keys required by the providers you use.

docs.title: MCP Tools & Resources
docs.text: mcp-searchable exposes a focused set of tools for agent-driven research.

docs.title: Available Tools
docs.text: Tool Parameters Description web_search query (string), provider (enum: duckduckgo, google, bing, brave), limit (positive integer, default: 5) Searches web providers and returns normalized results (title, url, snippet). web_fetch url (string) Fetches a URL and extracts Markdown content. web_stash url (string), title (string), content (string) Stores or updates a page in local SQLite storage. web_grep query (string), limit (positive integer, default: 5) Runs FTS5 search across stashed pages and returns ranked snippets. web_ask question (string), limit (positive integer, default: 3) Uses local Ollama with stashed context and returns answer + source URLs.

docs.title: Available Resources
docs.text: Currently, this server focuses on tools and does not expose additional MCP resource URIs.
